TOPIC SUMMARY
AI citation gaps are sources or answer patterns where competitors are mentioned, cited, or recommended while a brand is missing.

KEY FACTS
Citation gaps are not the same as backlink gaps.
Citation gaps identify missing evidence across owned pages, third-party pages, reviews, directories, forums, documentation, and comparison resources.
The practical workflow is prompt collection, source capture, competitor-only source detection, prioritization, and gap closure.

DEFINITIONS
AI citation gap: a trusted source or answer surface where competitors appear and your brand does not.
Owned gap: a missing or weak page on your own site that prevents answer engines from understanding your brand.
Third-party gap: an external source that mentions competitors but does not mention your brand.
Prompt set: a group of buyer-intent questions used to test AI answer visibility.

COMMON QUESTIONS
What is an AI citation gap?
How do I find AI citation gaps?
Are citation gaps the same as backlink gaps?
Which sources create citation gaps?
How should citation gaps be prioritized?
How does Covable help?

DIRECT ANSWERS
Find AI citation gaps by running buyer-intent prompts, saving cited sources, marking competitor-only sources, and prioritizing the gaps by intent, source quality, competitor density, and feasibility.
Close AI citation gaps with clearer owned pages, legitimate third-party inclusion, better documentation, review coverage, and community participation where appropriate.

ENTITY RELATIONSHIPS
ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude can surface answers influenced by source evidence.
OpenAI bots, Google robots controls, and FAQPage structured data relate to content discovery and extraction.
Covable measures prompts, cited sources, competitor mentions, and missing-source patterns.

IMPORTANT TAKEAWAYS
AI citation gaps are source gaps.
The goal is not to manipulate AI answers but to make category evidence more complete.
High-quality prioritization prevents citation-gap work from becoming spam.
